steps.title: Clean the stored brand names
steps.change: TRIM turns the padded Nike entry into Nike. A string of three spaces becomes an empty string. All eight product rows remain.
steps.sql: SELECT ProductID, Brand, TRIM(Brand) AS CleanBrand FROM Products ORDER BY ProductID;

steps.title: Remove missing and empty names
steps.change: Filtering removes products 3, 4 and 5. Nike and Adidas still appear twice.
steps.added_sql: WHERE TRIM(Brand) IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(Brand)) > 0
steps.sql: SELECT ProductID, TRIM(Brand) AS Brand FROM Products WHERE TRIM(Brand) IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(Brand)) > 0 ORDER BY ProductID;

steps.title: Keep each cleaned brand once
steps.change: The two Nike rows and two Adidas rows collapse to one of each. Three distinct brand names survive. Their order is still unspecified.
steps.sql: SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(Brand) AS Brand FROM Products WHERE TRIM(Brand) IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(Brand)) > 0;

steps.title: Sort the directory
steps.change: The output now has exactly one row per usable brand, alphabetically ordered from Adidas to Puma.
